activities.method: Builds the corridor model (Canada Water): a 10 m terrain grid, building footprints with heights, water levels, railways with tunnel chains and open cuts, roads, and stations and Wikidata places, in local metres around E0 535400, N0 179400.
rules: Terrain: median of the DTM in a 7 x 7 m window every 10 m.

Building height: OSM height tag; else the 90th percentile of DSM - DTM inside the footprint (at least 6 cells, at least 2 m) unless it is under half of building:levels x 3 m; else building:levels x 3 m + 1 m ('newer' when LiDAR exists); else the LiDAR value; else 6 m (0 for building=construction).
Buildings: centroid inside the box with a 2 m margin; single-outer multipolygons only.
Water: natural=water, waterway=dock or landuse=basin over 50 m2; level = 25th percentile of the DTM inside.
Tunnel portals: tunnel nodes shared with an open railway way, at the open track level (DSM on bridges, DTM otherwise).
Open cut: a tunnel point where the DTM is more than 6 m below the ground 25-35 m around; each run of cut points takes its lowest bed.
Published levels from data/sourced-levels.json are applied to the nearest tunnel point within 150 m (lib.mjs applyControls); superseded controls are skipped.
Places: OSM railway=station nodes, then Wikidata items of a fixed list of transport, water and landform classes that are not already a station.

used.request: two chart-datum-to-ODN offsets written into the code: 3.20 m at London Bridge, 3.35 m at North Woolwich

activities.method: Builds the Docklands 3D model (terrain, water, greens, buildings and parts, roads, railways, tunnels, places, flood defences, riverbed) into area.js, and the Canary Wharf underground detail (basements, indoor ways, level-tagged points, published structures) into under.js, in local metres around E0 537550, N0 180300.
rules: Terrain: median of the DTM in a 7 x 7 m window every 20 m.

Building height: OSM height; else LiDAR 90th percentile of DSM - DTM (at least 6 cells, at least 2 m) unless under half of building:levels x 3 m; else Wikidata P2048 (outlines only); else building:levels x 3 m + 1 m ('newer' when LiDAR exists); else LiDAR; else 6 m (0 for construction, roof, ruins).
An outline that contains building parts is drawn by its parts; a part's base is its min_height, else building:min_level x 3 m.
Outside the Canary Wharf focus box, outlines under 12 m2 are dropped and rings are simplified at 0.6 m (0.2 m inside).
Basements: OSM building:levels:underground, else Wikidata P1139.
Floors (focus box only): OSM building:levels (minus building:min_level on a part), else Wikidata P1101.
Water level: 25th percentile of the DTM inside the area; areas under 40 m2 (water) or 300 m2 (greens) are dropped.
Bridge points more than 20 m above the DTM are taken as covered by a roof and interpolated from the nearest uncovered points on the same way.
Tunnel chains for rail, road and foot tunnels; portals at the open level; open cut where the DTM is more than 6 m below the ground 25-35 m around.
Riverbed: each UKHO sounding in the box as z_cd minus the chart datum offset interpolated by longitude between 3.20 m and 3.35 m.
Flood defence crest: actual_ucl, else actual_dcl, else design_ucl; lines without a crest are dropped.
Published levels from data/sourced-levels.json are tunnel controls (nearest point within 150 m); structures with footprint_osm or water_name are drawn from their OSM way or water area.
Wikidata places: classes matching the KEEP pattern; classes matching memorial, war memorial, grave or cemetery are left out.
Level tags are read by tools/osm-values.mjs osmLevels.

activities.method: Merges the OSM, FSA, Wikidata, CWG directory and store-page evidence into one list of chain-store branches in the Canary Wharf box, with sources, position, mall, level and a confidence.
rules: Records join only when they are the same brand family (same Wikidata QID or a P749 parent, else same NSI id) and the same place: within 120 m (160 m when a position is approximate), or the same postcode, or the same mall.
Two named malls decide a join by themselves; Canada Place and One Canada Square count as one level.
An OSM feature whose fhrs:id equals the FSA premises id is the same branch.
Wikidata items join a branch within 300 m.

A CWG entry needs an NSI match (or a decision in cwg-decisions.json); a 'prefix' or 'alternate' match or a type that does not fit the CWG section is left undecided; otherwise a CWG title that names a branch already found (5 or more letters, whole words) joins it.
Postcode to mall: kept when 4 or more CWG entries share the postcode and 85% or more name the same mall.
Position: OSM feature, else FSA geocode, else mall centre or ONSPD postcode centroid (flagged).
Confidence: high with two or more sources; low for a single prefix or alternate FSA match or a note that says low confidence; else medium.
Category from the key=value (bank, pharmacy, supermarket, cafe, takeaway, restaurant, bar, gym, hotel, leisure, health, childcare, office, motoring, service, shop, other).

robots.txt per RFC 9309 (token glitchcan-cwplans, else *); an unreachable robots.txt means no visit; the failure is classed by its cause (dns, tls, timeout, 5xx).

activities.method: Cleans each JSON-LD block (jsonld-clean.mjs: wrappers, comments, trailing and missing commas, control characters, invalid escapes, concatenated values, HTML entities, remote schema.org contexts inlined as {"@vocab": "https://schema.org/"}, @graph unwrapped, http://schema.org/ normalised; every repair counted by class), converts it with Factoidal jsonldToRdf, converts microdata JSON to RDF (schema.org vocabulary), parses RDFa N-Triples with Factoidal, loads one named graph per page, writes all.nq, then runs SPARQL with Factoidal for types, names, telephones, opening hours and their specifications, addresses, geo and events, and attributes each node to the registry entities that link to the page.
rules: Scope branch, confidence high: the node's postcode equals the entity's, or its geo is within 300 m of the building.
Scope branch, confidence medium: the node has no address and the page is the branch's own page (a store_url field, a store-finder result, or a URL path that names the place).
Scope branch, confidence low: the node's postcode is another E14/E20 postcode (a sibling branch is possible).
Scope chain: a chain branch's general page with no address on the node (chain-wide facts, not branch facts). Scope organisation: the same for a non-chain entity's own site.
Nodes with an address or position elsewhere are not attributed and are counted.

Opening hours to OSM opening_hours: days grouped, 23:59 closes become 24:00, opens = closes = 00:00 is 'off', dated specifications become date-range rules; unparsed text is kept raw with the problem listed.

activities.method: Builds the Canary Wharf building registry: one record per OSM building outline with a stable cwb- id, its parts, occupants (OSM, FSA, Wikidata, chain-store branches, the Canary Wharf Group directory, the regulatory and public registers), owners, postcodes, Wikidata facts, and company and property joins.
rules: A building is an OSM building outline (way or multipolygon) whose vertex mean is in the Canary Wharf box; building:part shapes are listed under the outline that contains their centre.
Ids: reused from registry/ids.json by OSM element; new outlines get the next number in reading order (north to south in 100 m bands, then west to east); a retired id is never reused.

OSM occupants: named features with a shop, food and drink, office, amenity, leisure, tourism, healthcare, craft or transport role, placed in the outline that contains them or the nearest outline within 12 m; artworks, information boards, viewpoints and attractions are features, not occupants. Each OSM occupant keeps its tags opening_hours, cuisine, wheelchair, check_date, start_date, opening_date, operator, url, level, brand, brand:wikidata, website (or contact:website), phone (or contact:phone), email (or contact:email) and the other contact:* links (as contact).
FSA premises with a position in the box are placed the same way; the others are listed under their postcode when its tier is cw-*.

Wikidata: an OSM wikidata tag wins; else the one building-like item whose coordinate is in the outline (within 5 m) and no other building-like item is inside it; an item already named by an OSM tag is not attached to a second outline; other items inside are occupants 'located here'.
The Wikidata label replaces the OSM name; the OSM name is kept as osm_name.
Owners: Wikidata P127. Occupants also from P466 and from organisations whose P159 is the building.
UPRN points inside the outline (no tolerance) give UPRN counts, TOIDs and USRNs; LBSM2 homes are summed over the building's TOIDs.
Home figures are given only where at least 5 homes are counted (K = 5); otherwise 'fewer than 5'.
INSPIRE polygons that contain the building's centre are linked by INSPIRE id.

Companies and price-paid sales join a building when the postcode is one of its postcodes and the normalised address contains one of its keys (address, name, OSM name, Wikidata street address), and exactly one building matches.
A residential building lists only the count of registered companies, not their names.
Branches enrich the occupant with the same OSM or FSA id, else are placed by position (marked approximate when the position is a mall or postcode centre).
Buildings keep the OSM addr:housename (housename): it names the complex for a mall outline (Canada Place on 16-19 Canada Square).

CWG directory: an entry already linked by the branch join keeps that link. Else it joins existing occupants (OSM, FSA, Wikidata, branches, and CWG occupants added earlier in the same pass) when a name key is equal (registry/sources/brands/tools/cwg-fields.mjs nameKeys) and the place agrees, tried in this order: same mall (or same street or square), a shared postcode, or the building the entry itself would be placed in. Two different named malls never join (Canada Place and the One Canada Square mall count as one). An occupant with a CWG link takes a second entry only from another CWG section (cwg_also). Records of one source in two buildings: ambiguous, not joined.

CWG entries that join nothing become occupants (source cwg, role directory: <section>) placed by: the one building whose address key equals the street line (confidence high with the postcode, medium without); else the host outline of a named mall (the one outline whose OSM name, else addr:housename, is the mall name or starts with it; medium); else the one registry building with the entry postcode, or the one of them OSM tags as retail (low). Estate-wide entries, car parks and entries with no page, address or single building stay unplaced with a reason (cwg_unplaced, summary.joins.cwg).

Registers (registry/sources/registers/): records are excluded when the address is not a place: GIAS correspondence addresses (address_role), the registered-office service at E14 5HU / 10th floor 5 Churchill Place, care-of and accountant addresses. Keys in order: UPRN (OS Open UPRN point inside an outline; not used when one register gives the UPRN to records at two or more postcodes, or when the UPRN point is over 150 m from the register point), the register point (inside or within 12 m; an FSA point within 3 m of its postcode centre is a postcode, F7), a named mall in the address (the mall host outline, F4; the point outline kept as point_in), street address with the postcode, street address alone when one building matches a numbered address key, the name of an occupant at the same postcode or mall, the postcode alone when one registry building has it, the ONSPD centre is within 50 m of it and the address names no other street (never for a charity). A charity placed by address in a residential building (homes or a residential building tag) is left unplaced. A record whose name matches an occupant of the chosen building enriches it; else it is a new occupant (source = register, role register: <name> or head office (ODS) for ODS organisation records, current false for closed or inactive records). Each link (occupant.registers[]) keeps register, id, kind, status, key, precision, confidence; source ids are copied to the occupant (urn, ods_code, cqc_location_id, charity_number, company_number, ofsted_urn, gambling_premises_id, active_places_site_id, fhrs_id). Unplaced records and rejected UPRNs are listed (registers_unplaced, registers_uprn_rejected).

rules: Keys: "cwb-NNNN|name" (occupant name in that building, case and accents folded), "branch:<brand QID>@<element>" (the occupant's OSM element, the building's OSM way, fhrs/<FSA id> or a bare FSA id, cwg/<slug>), "charity:<number>", "cwg:<directory slug>".
One record per occupant: branch scope beats organisation beats chain; then high, medium, low confidence.
A fact record with no hours, phone, events, menu, price range or cuisine is not joined; records that match no occupant are counted (summary.joins.web_facts).
Run after build-registry (which rewrites buildings.json without web facts) and before build-categories and build-atlas.

activities.method: Gives each registry building its occupant categories (finance, shop, catering, leisure, entertainment; and bar, alcohol, education, health, sport, arts, charity) from the classes the sources state, for the glow outlines and the atlas.
rules: finance: OSM amenity bank, bureau_de_change or money_transfer, or office financial, insurance, financial_advisor or tax_advisor; or a Wikidata P31 or P452 label matching bank, finance, insurance, investment and similar; or the role 'service: bank' or 'branch: bank'.
shop: an OSM shop tag, the role 'shop' or 'branch: shop', or an FSA type starting 'Retailers'.
catering: OSM amenity restaurant, cafe, bar, pub, fast_food, food_court, ice_cream or biergarten; the role 'food and drink' or a food branch; or an FSA catering type.
leisure: OSM leisure fitness_centre, sports_centre, swimming_pool, sauna, dance or sports_hall; a hotel role or FSA hotel type.
entertainment: OSM cinema, theatre, nightclub, arts centre, casino, events or music venue, planetarium, amusement and bowling leisure, museum or gallery; or a Wikidata class matching those.
bar: OSM amenity pub, bar, nightclub or biergarten; FSA type Pub/bar/nightclub; CWG category Bars or Cocktails; a Wikidata class pub, bar, nightclub.
alcohol: OSM shop alcohol, wine or beverages.

education: OSM amenity school, college, university, kindergarten or childcare; FSA type School/college/university; CWG category Childcare; a Wikidata class school, university, college, academic institution, kindergarten or nursery; the role branch: childcare.

health: OSM amenity doctors, dentist, pharmacy, clinic or hospital, or any healthcare tag; CWG category Healthcare unless OSM says amenity=veterinary; a Wikidata class hospital, clinic, doctor's office, medical organization, dental, pharmacy.

sport: OSM leisure sports_centre, fitness_centre, pitch, swimming_pool or sports_hall, or any sport tag; CWG category Sport (not Sport & Fitness, which lists sportswear shops); a Wikidata sports venue or gym class; the role branch: gym.

arts: OSM amenity cinema, theatre, arts_centre, nightclub, music_venue, events_venue or concert_hall, or any theatre:genre tag; a Wikidata class movie theater, cinema, theatre, music venue, concert hall, arts centre or nightclub.

CWG directory classes for the first five: section restaurant gives catering, section stay or category Hotels & Apartments gives leisure, category Banks & Foreign Exchange gives finance, and goods categories (Shoes & Footwear, Menswear, Jewellery & Watches and others listed in the tool) give shop. CWG labels that mix classes (Services, Health & Beauty, Cafes & Bars, Sport & Fitness) and the FSA type Hospitals/Childcare/Caring Premises are not used.

Registers (current links only): GIAS, Ofsted childcare and ODS School give education; CQC health services (doctors, dentists, diagnosis, urgent care, clinics, hospitals, community healthcare, nursing homes) and ODS service sites (pharmacies, surgeries, GP practices, dental practices, optical sites, NHS trust, independent provider, PCT and care trust sites) give health; Active Places gives sport; FSA pubs give bar; gambling premises (betting shops) give shop; the Charity Commission gives charity. ODS organisation records, ODS Education (NHS training bodies) and social care services give no category. An occupant with current false counts as former.
Names are never used to guess a class; Companies House registered offices are not used.

Wikidata occupant links: an end date (P582) or a dissolved organisation (P576) makes the entry 'former' and it is not counted; a start date and no end makes it 'current'; no qualifier makes it 'undated'.

activities.method: Builds the compact index the atlas page loads first: buildings with outlines and model heights, postcodes with company and home totals, heritage groups, riverbed soundings, wrecks, flood defences, Wikidata items, published levels and overview counts.

Levels: the sourced levels used by the 3D build, CWG structures (slabs, water, dock bed), the deepest and median sounding off the Isle of Dogs, and the 8 tallest named buildings (Wikidata, else OSM, else LiDAR height on the LiDAR ground, or 5 m OD when unknown, marked approx).

activities.method: Builds the Canary Wharf walking network in 3D from OSM (footways, corridors, stairs, escalators, lifts, platforms, streets) with each point on its level, adds TfL's step-free station topology, attaches named places, and records faults for the audit.
rules: Box -0.0330, 51.4960 to -0.0020, 51.5120; walkable highway values, not access=private or foot=no, plus platforms, conveying ways and indoor areas, corridors and rooms.
Level: level, else level:ref (tools/osm-values.mjs osmLevels), else layer when the way is a tunnel, indoor or underground with layer < 0, else 0.
One vertex per (OSM node, level); stairs and escalators are oriented by the levels their ends touch, else by incline, else counted as unresolved.
A lift node joins its copies at the levels it lists, in order.
Walkable areas get a hub joined to every vertex on their level inside them or within 3 m of their edge.
A node that ordinary ways reach at two levels with no connector is joined as 'ramp' and counted as a level jump.

TfL points join the nearest OSM vertex within 35 m only at street level (TfL level 0 = OSM level 0); TfL lifts (pathway_mode 5) and paths join TfL points; nearest-vertex level pairs are recorded per station.
Places attach to the nearest vertex on their own level within 40 m, else the nearest vertex on any level within 40 m (marked).

activities.method: Fits tiered massing (stacked flat tiers, or a pyramid, cone or sloped top where that fits clearly better) to the towers of 100 m or more, from the 1 m EA LiDAR surface model, for the 3D page.
rules: Primary survey: the 2022 composite (flights of 2017-12 to 2018-01 and 2020-12-12); the 2018 flight where judgement says so (Novotel, Dollar Bay: under half their roof cells returned in 2020).
Dropouts (8 m under the 75th percentile of their 5 x 5 m) filled by a 3 x 3 m grey closing.
OSM outline shifted by whole metres (at most 4) onto the LiDAR building.
Roof levels: 1-D Gaussian mixture, k by BIC + 2 k ln n; levels closer than 3 m merge.
Outlines: open and close, holes under 60 m2 filled, pieces under 16 m2 removed, marching squares, Douglas-Peucker 0.8 m, edges snapped to the dominant direction within 8 degrees.
Towers not standing at the 2020 flight keep their OSM outline (status not_in_survey).
Hand corrections are listed in the tool (JUDGEMENT) and in each record with its reason.

Periods by autocorrelation of gradient profiles, FFT cross-check; the fundamental chosen by looking at the patch.
Colours: k-means, k = 3, in Lab.

activities.method: Writes the rectified patches at metric aspect and the bays, floors and colours in metres.

activities.method: Joins the measurements, the footprint widths and the judged facts into one record per tower, each value marked measured, judged or assumed.

activities.method: Cuts one tile per tower from its rectified open photo, holding whole floors and whole bays so it repeats along the walls, and packs the tiles into an 8 x 4 atlas of 256 px tiles.
rules: One patch per tower, chosen by eye from data/raw/facades/contact.jpg; Citigroup Centre left out (crane, blur).
Tile = whole floors (about 40% of the patch, at most 25 m) by whole bays; size in metres from the measured floor height or bay width.
Attribution per tile from photos.json.

activities.method: Synthesises Gaussian splats straight from the model (no training): ground discs coloured from the 2008 aerial photograph, roof discs, and wall discs with a glass band, written as .splat and as a 3DGS PLY.
rules: Box: the model's focus box plus 300 m unless --box is given.
Ground discs every 4 m (--ground) where no building covers the cell, coloured bilinearly from rgb2008.ppm.
Roof discs every 4 m inside the outline: aerial colour on buildings under 40 m, else the building colour.
Walls: one disc per 3.6 m storey and 7.2 m (--cell) of wall, and one glass-band disc 3 cm in front per cell (buildings 4 m or taller).
The set entry 'cw-synth' replaces any earlier one in index.json; other entries are kept.

activities.method: Joins the tree inventories, OSM trees and the Trees Outside Woodland lone-tree crowns into one list of trees in model metres, with OS Open Greenspace sites, OSM green areas and TOW canopy groups as green rings.
rules: Box: BNG E 532400-539900, N 176700-182300 (fetch-docklands.mjs BOX_BNG); WGS84 to BNG through OSTN15; x = E - 537550, z = -(N - 180300); every value rounded to 0.5 m.

Ethics (CLAUDE.md, Data ethics): a tree keeps only position, taxon (scientific and common name), height, crown spread, source and record id. Notes, sponsorship, memorial, dedication, inscription, address, owner and maintainer fields are never read into the payload; each source lists its dropped fields in sources[].dropped.

Tree precedence: GLA public realm inventory first; then TPO points (planning.data), OSM natural=tree nodes and TOW Lone Tree crowns, each added only if no tree already kept lies within 3 m (TOW: within the crown radius, at least 3 m).
GLA class values ("05 to 10 m") become the middle of the class; "Not recorded" is null. Species "Unknown Tree Species" and common name "Plant" give no species.
TPO: records with an end date are left out; the taxon is read only from Tower Hamlets names of the form "Common (Scientific)"; Southwark names (site descriptions, URLs) are dropped.
OSM: species, else taxon, else genus (with the :en names); height under 60 m and diameter_crown under 40 m kept.
TOW Lone Tree: centroid of the polygon, height = maxht, crown = diameter of a circle with the polygon area (tow_area_m). Group of Trees, Small Woodland and NFI OHC polygons become greens with meanht.

Greens are clipped to the box (Sutherland-Hodgman) and simplified (Douglas-Peucker 0.5 m; TOW 1.5 m, its outlines follow the 1 m LiDAR grid); OSM multipolygon inner rings and shapefile holes are kept as holes.

activities.method: Converts a 3DGS PLY to the antimatter15 32-byte .splat format.
rules: scale = exp(log scale); rgb = 0.5 + SH_C0 x f_dc; alpha = sigmoid(opacity); quaternion normalised and stored as q x 128 + 128.
Sorted by exp(sum of log scales) x opacity, largest first; non-finite gaussians are dropped; f_rest is ignored.

activities.method: Puts a trained splat set on the 3D page: crops it to the area the drone frames cover, drops floaters and oversized splats, and gives each splat its model building for the music visualiser.
rules: Keep splats within the box of the frame positions plus 150 m, between -30 and 260 m OD, with no axis over 25 m.
A splat belongs to a building when it lies inside the footprint (2 m grace) between the base - 2 m and the top + 6 m; else 65535.
Positions are not changed: train-splat.sh keeps the model frame (no --center).

activities.method: Runs 39 data-quality checks over every Canary Wharf source (identity, spatial, attribute, validity, parsing, network, timeliness, coverage, semantics) and writes one record per issue with counts, rates and examples, and a generated Markdown catalogue.
rules: Checks ID-1 to ID-5, SP-1 to SP-7, AT-1 to AT-5, VA-1 to VA-4, PL-1, PL-2, NET-1 to NET-5, TM-1 to TM-4, CV-1 to CV-4, SE-1 to SE-3.
The audit date is fixed in the code (2026-10-03): FSA ratings before 2023-10-03 are 'older than 3 years'; CWG copy ages are counted to that date.
VA-2 issues are the level tokens tools/osm-values.mjs cannot read (osmLevelsUnread).
Each issue has a severity (high, medium, low) and an entity (building, postcode, OSM element, FSA premises and others).

SP-2 leaves out occupants placed by a key (placed_confidence: SP-7). SP-6 counts an outline as the mall when its name, OSM name or addr:housename names it. CV-2 counts a CWG entry as seen by another source when a registry occupant from another source carries its URL after the registry join. CV-3: CWG entries the registry could not place, by reason.

CV-4: register records in the registry box with no building, by reason; ID-5: register UPRNs not used (shared across postcodes, or far from the register point); SE-3: register addresses that are not where the organisation works.
